reason: H0 exercises only the linear decode_image_config → decode_frame_config → decode_frame protocol. It never calls restart_frame!, so it cannot test whether restarting correctly resets expect_multiple_scans before a subsequent scan is processed. This is material because S1 explicitly adds expect_multiple_scans state, uses it in decode_sos? to return "#bad scan count", derives it in prepare_scan?, and resets it in restart_frame!.
evidence: fuzz_image_decoder calls wuffs_base__image_decoder__decode_image_config, then repeatedly calls decode_frame_config and decode_frame; no restart_frame call appears.
S1 decoder.prepare_scan? assigns expect_multiple_scans when scan_count == 0 based on sof_marker and component counts.
S1 decoder.decode_sos? rejects scan_count > 0 when expect_multiple_scans is false.
S1 decoder.restart_frame! newly sets expect_multiple_scans = false and scan_count = 0, establishing restart-specific state behavior absent from H0.
recommended_action: Add a fuzz path that, after reaching a valid frame state, calls restart_frame!(index: 0, io_position: a fuzz-selected valid position), repositions or reconstructs the input buffer consistently, and continues through decode_frame_config and decode_frame. Vary JPEGs whose first scan does and does not set expect_multiple_scans, and also exercise invalid restart index and call-sequence cases.
